public_rationale: Under the ordinary task-level meaning of automation, the categorical statement is contradicted. Intercom reported deployed Fin systems resolving customer questions in April 2024, and its technical description identifies GPT-4 as part of the system. Customer feedback exposes problems with counting assumed resolutions, so 46% should not be treated as a verified success rate. Those problems do not erase the evidence that some questions were answered successfully without a human agent.
limitations: The main quantitative evidence comes from the vendor.
The customer account is anecdotal, not a controlled evaluation.
This does not establish reliable automation of whole jobs or complex workflows.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of mid-2024, generative AI does not actually work as automation.

statement.excerpt: Here's the thing, I get that that might be what they're pushing toward, but generative AI isn't even automation at this point.
statement.document_title: Rot Economics - An Interview With MIT's Daron Acemoglu

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that generative AI was not successfully performing real work tasks without a person executing each task.
Automation can cover a bounded task, including answering customer questions. It need not replace an entire occupation or work without errors.
For this ongoing observation, use April–June 2024, the latest complete quarter before publication.
criteria.support_condition: Representative deployment evidence establishes that purported generative AI automation still required humans to perform the tasks, with no credible working counterexample.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented deployment in the target period successfully performs a real work task using generative AI without human execution of each instance.
